newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SEMICONDUCTORS ERODE PHILIPS BOTTOM LINE.
newsitem.headline: SEMICONDUCTORS ERODE PHILIPS BOTTOM LINE.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday ongoing price pressure in semiconductors had fed straight through to its bottom line.
"Price erosion (in the semi-conductors industry) has increased from two percent in 1995 to eight percent in 1996," finance director Dudley Eustace told a results news conference.
Given the high fixed costs in semi-conductors, most of the price deterioration had gone directly to the bottom line, he said.
Philips' other businesses had been unable to take up the slack in profit, he added.
The company earlier announced third quarter ordinary net profits of 123 million guilders, sharply down from a year-earlier 539 million.
The components and semi-conductors division posted nine-month operating income of 1.19 billion guilders, down from 1.7 billion in the first nine months of 1995.

Eustace said there were tentative signals of a possible recovery. "Book-to-Bill ratios...now show levels last seen in January of this year, but it's probably still too early to be able to confirm a new trend."
Book-to-bill ratios would have to show at least two or three months of sustained improvement before a recovery could be confidently predicted, he said.
"When you're sitting in the bottom of a pit, it seems a long way up...but we hope to be doing better in the fourth quarter, he said.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000.
